tasks.short: Consult users and vendors, then assess computing needs.

steps.what: Consult users, management, vendors, and technicians
List current systems from the inventory
Assess computing needs and system requirements

outputs: filed copy of signed needs assessment v1

tasks.design: The inventory on {DATA_PLATFORM} lists current systems. The manager consults users, management, vendors, and technicians, assesses computing needs, signs the assessment in {DOCS}, and a job files that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were gathered in calls that never met the inventory.
tasks.enabler_now: The inventory can be listed without a new platform.
tasks.still_hard: A vendor's claim still has to be judged against the work.

ambition.what: Attach the current inventory to a needs note before it is signed.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the consultation on the requirement, not on listing systems.

evidence.claim: The management digest says security and IT work uses ticket and incident-log configuration, and judgement stays manual.
The management digest says a records path can draft a report that cites record ids, and a person signs.

assumptions: The list is the inventory, not a recommendation.
Configure the inventory before a new store.
unknowns: Which needs become a funded change.
research_questions: How often the inventory misses a local tool.

already_counted.description: The consultation stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only assembly and filing move to a job. The meeting, the decision, and the signature stay with the manager, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and interpret goals, policies, and procedures.

steps.what: Develop organizational goals, policies, and procedures
Draft policy sentences from the manager's outline

loop.purpose: Draft policy prose from the outline only
loop.check: every duty is one the outline already states
loop.stop: one draft, or stop when a duty is not in the outline
loop.why_not_simpler: the wording changes with the goal, so a fixed clause does not fit

steps.what: Interpret the policies against current practice

outputs: filed copy of signed policy v1

tasks.design: The manager develops the goals and policies. A bounded draft in {DOCS} may phrase only what the outline already says. The manager interprets the policy against practice, signs that version, and a job files it. The draft is not the policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were rewritten from the last version, and a new duty could appear with no owner.
tasks.enabler_now: An outline can constrain a draft without a new platform.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting a policy for this organisation is still the manager's job.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the goal and what the policy means in practice.
tasks.altitude: The manager still sets the policy. Phrasing and filing shrink.

evidence.claim: The management digest says a records path can draft a report that cites record ids, and a person signs.
Digest [S14] requires works-council consent for hiring, appraisal, staff data, or monitoring unless a collective agreement settles it, so this design does not add a watch or a score.

assumptions: A duty that is not in the outline is removed before signature.
Configure the document store before a new tool.
unknowns: Who else must sign a policy.
Whether staff representatives must see it first.
research_questions: How a signed policy is withdrawn.

already_counted.description: Developing and interpreting the policy stay inside the remaining time of those steps.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

tasks.short: Evaluate technology use and recommend hardware or software upgrades.

steps.what: Evaluate the organization's technology use and needs
List hardware and software versions from the inventory
Recommend improvements such as hardware upgrades

outputs: filed copy of signed upgrade recommendation v1

tasks.design: A job lists hardware and software versions from {DATA_PLATFORM}. The manager evaluates use and needs, recommends the improvement, signs it in {DOCS}, and a job files that version. The job does not buy or install anything.
tasks.previous_blocker: Version lists were stale, so a recommendation could name a release nobody still ran.
tasks.enabler_now: The inventory can list versions without a new platform.
tasks.still_hard: Whether an upgrade is worth the disruption is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recommends the change and stands behind it.

ambition.what: Refresh the version list before an upgrade recommendation is signed.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the evaluation on the need, not on collecting versions.

unknowns: Who may approve spend on an upgrade.
Which systems are in the inventory.
research_questions: How often local installs are missing from the inventory.

tasks.short: Review and approve systems charts and programs before implementation.

steps.what: Review systems charts and programs before implementation
Approve programs prior to their implementation

outputs: filed copy of signed program approval v1

tasks.design: The manager reviews the systems charts and programs and approves them prior to implementation. A job files that approval in {DOCS}. It does not implement the program or change a live system. A new version voids the approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval was a mail reply that did not name the version.
tasks.enabler_now: The document store can hold a versioned approval.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the program and deciding it is fit still takes the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager approves or refuses that version, and implementation stays a separate human release.
tasks.altitude: The review does not shrink. Filing the signed approval does.

reach.task: Implement only the version the manager approved

evidence.claim: The management digest says security and IT work uses ticket and incident-log configuration, and judgement stays manual.
The management digest says a records path can draft a report that cites record ids, and a person signs.

assumptions: The job never applies a change to a live system.
A changed program needs a new signature.
unknowns: Who else must approve before implementation.
Where the canonical charts are kept.
research_questions: How implementation is evidenced after this approval.

role.altitude: The information systems manager spends the week on priorities, people, and the signed decision. Ticket totals and filing a signed note move to a job. A backup that already runs is not saved labour.
reach: Service desk leads receive a signed priority list instead of a verbal shuffle.
Analysts see the assignment the manager signed, not a score.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report figure that has no ticket or ledger row.
Keep hiring, assignment, and access changes as their own decision.
role.ambitious_version: A signed priority list can open the week's work board, and the manager still releases it.
